text:
chris: Hey team — hitting a streaming issue where after client reconnect the last JSON object is cut off and there9s no finish_reason. Repro steps below, happening on hosted API and on our dedicated instance

chris: curl reproduce (trimmed)
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\ 
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\ 
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-2.1\" 
```

chris: Sequence: request starts -> partial tokens stream -> client disconnects (mobile sleep) -> client reconnects with resume header -> stream resumes but final object ends with truncated JSON like `... \"content\": \"...` and no finish_reason key

maya: sorry, annoying. can you paste the exact final bytes you see? single-line is fine

chris: last bytes (exact):
```
data: {"id":"res_abc","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...and that
"},"index":0,"finish_reason":null}]}

data: {"id":"res_abc","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"more text but abruptly cut"},"index":0}]}
```


chris: then connection closes. the final line the client gets is `more text but abruptly cut` — there9s no trailing `}` to close the outer object sometimes, and other times finish_reason is completely absent instead of `stop`

support-bot: Thanks for reporting. Tagging eng-oncall. Please include client library/version, proxy, and whether you see `Resume-Range` header on reconnect.

eng-oncall: @chris can you confirm if you9re using the resume token header `x-redwood-resume` or only using TCP reconnect? Also which proxy sits in front (fastly/nginx/our edge)?

chris: Using our iOS client v1.4.2. We attach `x-redwood-resume: <token>` on reconnect. Traffic goes through CloudFront -> internal nginx -> redwood edge. We9ve seen same behaviour when skipping CloudFront (direct to nginx).

maya: quick hypothesis: the final event might be split across two TCP segments and our reconnect handler is replaying only up to last complete SSE event. Could be header mismatch on resume that prevents server from flushing the terminal sentinel. Can you share request/response headers around reconnect (no secrets)?

chris: headers (sanitized):
```
:method: GET
:authority: api.redwood.ai
:accept: text/event-stream
:authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
:x-redwood-resume: token=eyJ...
:connection: keep-alive
```

chris: server logs show: `stream-resume: token validated, replaying from offset=48231` then ~200ms later `connection closed by upstream (ECONNRESET)` and no `stream-finish` log.

eng-oncall: can you try a repro with `--no-buffer` or a tiny delay to force flush on server side? also does the client emit any TCP-level FIN or RST before reconnect?

chris: client logs: shows TCP FIN then immediate reconnect. we tried adding 200ms wait before reconnect -> improved in ~60% cases (final chunk appears), still flakey though.

maya: thanks. two tracks: 1) we'll add more guardrails in the resume path so server emits explicit terminal event before closing connection if it has already completed the response. 2) please share a minimal clipped capture (pcap or stdout trace) showing the exact bytes around the reconnect and I9ll escalate to runtime team.

chris: attaching a short tcpdump snippet inline (sanitized):
```
...
SYN/ACK handshake
GET /v1/streams?model=redwood-2.1 HTTP/1.1
[...event-stream data...]
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"final sentence part 1"}}]}
<client FIN>
<client reconnect> with x-redwood-resume
...
server sends: data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"part 2"}}]}
server stops without sending blank line separator or final finish_reason event
```

eng-oncall: helpful. tagging eng-runtime for kernel/flush checks. @maya pls include this thread in the escalation. Also, what9s the priority?

maya: P1 for customer-facing regressions. I9m opening an internal ticket and will post the ticket id here.

support-bot: Internal ticket created: RINF-8342. Assigned to eng-runtime. Please add any additional traces to the ticket.

chris: thanks. one more datapoint: if we disable `x-redwood-resume` and let client fully re-request without resume, the server always returns a clean final object (albeit duplicated tokens). So resume path specifically seems suspect.

maya: noted. that narrows it. eng-runtime, can you look at resume replay + connection close path for missing terminal sentinel emission? Also check behavior when upstream (nginx) issues a reset during replay.

eng-oncall: will do. for now, chris, adding client-side 200ms backoff on reconnect is a decent mitigation. we9ll follow up in RINF-8342 with root cause and a fix ETA.

chris: confirmed mitigation reduces incidence to ~5% in our tests. thanks, will attach additional traces to the ticket and follow up if it spikes.
